title: Net-90 Terms After the CFO-Approval Policy Took Effect
scenario_text:
A deal desk analyst at Pennington Cloud must decide how to handle an extended payment-term request, given how a similar request was handled last year.

**Decision A (2023-08)**
Customer 'Halden Freight' | 2-year deal | ARR $220K. Requested Net-90 (standard is Net-30). The regional Sales Director approved it directly. Note at the time: 'Directors may approve up to Net-90 at their discretion for strategic logos.'

**Current request C (2024-03-19)**
Customer 'Marlowe Systems' | 2-year deal | ARR $310K. Requesting Net-90. The AE has attached the Halden approval as supporting evidence.

**Payment Terms Policy (current, effective 2024-01-01)**
Any payment terms beyond Net-45 now require CFO approval. Sales Directors may approve up to Net-45 only. There is no ARR floor for CFO review, and CFO exceptions remain available for terms up to Net-90 with a documented business justification. The prior director-discretion authority for Net-90 was retired when this policy took effect.

**Slack — #deal-desk**
AE: 'We gave Halden Net-90 last year on the Director's sign-off, so Marlowe should just get the same. Let's not overcomplicate it.'
Analyst: 'Halden closed in August — that was before the January terms policy. Let me confirm who can actually approve Net-90 now.'

The AE is pushing to close before quarter-end and wants the analyst to grant Net-90 under the Director's authority to avoid the CFO queue. No CFO exception has been requested yet, and the business justification field on the Marlowe deal is currently blank.
question: How should the analyst handle Marlowe Systems' Net-90 request?
choices: Grant Net-90 under the Sales Director's authority, citing the Halden Freight approval as established precedent for strategic logos.

Route the Net-90 request to the CFO for exception review with a documented business justification, because the Halden approval predates the January 1, 2024 policy that retired director discretion for terms beyond Net-45.
Offer Net-45 as a compromise so the deal stays within the Sales Director's current authority and avoids CFO escalation entirely.
Deny the Net-90 request outright, since terms beyond Net-45 are no longer permitted at Pennington Cloud.
